title: Foundation is root's charge (howto)
desc: The protocol for keeping foundation work on ROOT: the test, the category line, the triple-reflex.
steps: THE ONE TEST before delegating ANYTHING: does this shape how other intelligences THINK or what they STAND ON? If YES it is the FOUNDATION -- keep it on ROOT and do it yourself with full care. Delegating the foundation to the intelligences that depend on it INVERTS the hierarchy.

CATEGORY LINE: CHORE = mechanical, replaceable, shapes nothing downstream (grep, parse-verify, file string edits, log scans) -> delegate to Agent.cmd. FOUNDATION = harness enforcement, on-load/Require wiring, the constitution, knowledge-architecture, reflex-pushing, recurrence-prevention -> ROOT does it directly.

TRIPLE REFLEX after EVERY user correction (not just a fix): (1) FIX the immediate issue, (2) KNOWLEDGE-IFY it into a skill + an action-first reflex, (3) EMBODY it in the harness so it SELF-ENFORCES (a guard, an enforcer read, a push onto the wire the next agent trips). A fix alone repeats; a skill alone is pull; only harness-embodiment makes it permanent + human-free. DONE TEST: would the next FRESH model hit this correction automatically without the user saying anything?
OVERCOMING: the moment you catch yourself labeling foundational/harness/knowledge-wiring work as a chore to offload, STOP -- that impulse IS the enemy; reclaim the task.

DELEGATION BOUNDARY: skill authoring + cross-linking REQUIRE high intelligence + ARE the foundation -> OPUS does them directly; delegate only read-only survey, parse-verify, guard-message strings, and mechanical residue.

INCIDENT: the FOURTH correction of this mistake, 2026-09-05 (and a FIFTH on 2026-09-12 through the stall guard: a pace-shaped refusal is even more misleading than a permission-shaped one -- it says nothing about who may touch the file, so a session reads its remedy as a routing instruction when it is only a throttle; the correct response to a stall refusal is to WAIT, to knowledge-ify, or to take a user turn; it is never to hand the merge down), and this time the rule was quoted CORRECTLY minutes before being broken -- so recitation is now proven insufficient and the trigger is named. WHEN: a guard refuses YOU and its refusal text names delegation as the remedy, which is the one shape that makes handing the work down feel like obedience. HOW: run wkappbot skill read post-compaction-recovery for the sibling record of this exact drift, then treat the guard's prescription as a TASK LIKE ANY OTHER and re-ask WHO before doing WHAT -- and where the answer is that only ROOT may do it, the correct response to the refusal is to STOP CREATING that artifact, never to hand the key to a cheaper tier. WHY: measured today. The omega-tier guard refused ROOT a plain cp of a verified proto onto its canonical path with the words hand it to a sector for wiring, or dispatch via Agent.cmd --model haiku. I dispatched. Minutes earlier, challenged by the owner, I had quoted step 7 of this very skill from memory and correctly -- proto to the cheap tier, canonical merge to ROOT, never ask the cheap model to touch the live file. Knowing it changed nothing, because the guard supplied the WHAT so convincingly that the WHO went unexamined. AND THE OWNER NAMED THE SECURITY CONSEQUENCE THE RULE EXISTS FOR: a delegate handed canonical write access can corrupt the wiring, and the byte-diff control does not catch it -- if the agent edits the .tmp proto as well, the diff comes back empty while the content is no longer what ROOT approved, and for a BRAND NEW file there is no canonical to diff against at all. So the diff proves copying, never fidelity to what was reviewed. THE RULE THAT SURVIVES: ROOT writes canonical or canonical does not get written, and a refusal that offers delegation as its remedy is offering the one exit this skill forbids. //why:Monitor refused, background task wakes me instead //why:ROOT owns wiring canonical files not delegation //why:ROOT owns wiring canonical files not delegation-haiku
